gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histological and/or molecular confirmation of glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: This phase II trial compares the effect of short course radiotherapy (RT) to standard course RT for the treatment of patients diagnosed with glioblastoma (GBM).
Patients also receive temozolomide PO on days 1-5 every 28 days during radiation therapy.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: To demonstrate non-inferior 12-month overall survival (OS) of patients with GBM treated with dose escalated hypofractionated radiotherapy compared to standard of care.

role_evidence.quote: Patients also receive temozolomide PO on days 1-5 every 28 days during radiation therapy.
Patients also receive temozolomide PO QD concurrently with radiation therapy and for up to 6 adjuvant cycles in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
Patients undergo PET/CT with 18-F-DOPA administered IV prior to RT on study

agents.drug_class_hint: fluorine-18 PET imaging tracer (18F-DOPA) for target volume delineation

coder_notes: Radiotherapy fractionation trial (short-course vs standard RT); no investigational drug. Temozolomide is given in both arms but on a different schedule (days 1-5 q28d during short-course RT vs daily concurrent in standard arm), so per R2 coded established_therapy_experiment rather than soc_backbone; the trial's question is RT fractionation, so the S6 reason could alternatively be no_pharmacological_candidate - either way no candidate. IDH-mutant tumours excluded (IDH-wildtype requirement) -> cns5; IDH is diagnostic only. 18F-DOPA PET is a registered drug intervention given to all patients, coded diagnostic_agent. Lymphocyte count and immune phenotyping relate to radiotherapy, not a drug candidate.
